examples.japanese: {足指|あしゆび}をぶつけて{痛|いた}い。
examples.english: I stubbed my toe and it hurts.

examples.japanese: {足指|あしゆび}を{広|ひろ}げるストレッチをしている。
{冬|ふゆ}になると{足指|あしゆび}が{冷|ひ}えて{感覚|かんかく}がなくなることがある。
examples.english: In winter, my toes sometimes get so cold that I lose feeling in them.

notes:
A compound of {足|あし} (foot, leg) + {指|ゆび} (finger, digit). Japanese uses {指|ゆび} for both fingers and toes, so {足指|あしゆび} specifies the toes. Also written as {足|あし}の{指|ゆび} in everyday speech.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {足指|あしゆび}を{動|うご}かす — move one's toes
- {足指|あしゆび}が{冷|ひ}える — toes get cold
- {足指|あしゆび}の{間|あいだ} — between the toes
- {足指|あしゆび}の{爪|つめ} — toenails

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {手指|てゆび}/{手|て}の{指|ゆび} — finger; the hand counterpart, specifying fingers rather than toes
- {指|ゆび} — finger/toe; the general word that covers both, with context determining which
- つま{先|さき} — tip of the toes, tiptoe; refers to the front end of the foot rather than individual toes
